notes.share_measure: shares are percentages built from domain_days (the month's mean daily share); the MIN_DEN floor applies to the peak-day denominator. domains_peak is not additive across values: se 2019-06 NSEC3 per-value peaks sum to 115% of the _total peak while zones moved from 1 to 5 iterations. Sums over several algorithm values still count a zone or delegation carrying two of them twice (rollovers), which can push a summed share slightly above 100.
notes.step_test: primary Q1/Q2 statistic: mean of actual minus a linear trend fitted to the 24 months before the event and extrapolated over the 12 months after. The centred rolling-median detrend absorbs a lasting level step, so the old statistic is kept only as a secondary transient-deviation test.
notes.strict_panel: every reverse share uses _pooled-afrinic-arin from out/panel_run; per-RIR server-run series are used only for counts (q4 spikes)
notes.reverse_dating: Every reverse source, the server run, the panel run and the ledger, uses one convention since the server run was relabelled: label M is the state at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of M. A reverse state difference or ledger change labelled M therefore happened during calendar month M-1. For a release in calendar month r, states up to label r are before it, after-states start at label r+1, and ledger changes after it are labels r+1 on. Forward labels are calendar months of measurement. No shift is applied to any series; the event index is moved instead (checked in q4.reverse_dating_check).
notes.forward_note: Forward corpus: earlier work found every forward adoption jump belonged to one of two registry operators, paired across that operator's TLDs, so a forward event study measures whether about a dozen organisations moved, not whether a market responded.
notes.release_dates: stable release row's `released` from data/software/timelines; default rows use Phase 4 timing_* columns, which already apply first_public_tag

q1_per_program_releases.method: Event = each stable, publicly shipped release, one per calendar month per program. Primary statistic step12: the mean over the 12 after-months of the share minus a linear trend fitted to the 24 before-months and extrapolated; it keeps a lasting level shift. Secondary statistic transient3, the transient deviation: mean detrended share over 3 after-months minus 3 before-months, detrended by a centred 25-month rolling median, which absorbs any lasting step. Reverse dating: for a release in calendar month r, before = labels <= r and after = labels r+1 on. Program statistic = mean over tested release months. Null: the release months that fall inside the series' own testable window circularly shifted by one uniform offset within that window, 1000 draws. A test needs a window of at least 24 months with release months filling at most 75% of it; otherwise every shift covers nearly the same months. Single-release band: 5th-95th percentile of the statistic over every testable month of the series.

q2_default_change_events.method: For each mapped default row and corpus. Primary, step12: mean over the 12 after-months of the share minus a linear trend fitted to the 24 before-months and extrapolated. Secondary, transient12, the transient deviation: detrended mean of 12 after-months minus 12 before-months, blind to a lasting step. Event month m = calendar month of the row's timing_date; forward after-months start at m, reverse after-labels start at m+1 because a reverse label is the state on the 1st. Null: 1000 placebo event months drawn with replacement from every eligible month of the same series; band = 5th-95th percentile. Benjamini-Hochberg q over each family. 'no test' where the series lacks the before- or after-period.
q2_default_change_events.forward_note: Forward corpus: earlier work found every forward adoption jump belonged to one of two registry operators, paired across that operator's TLDs, so a forward event study measures whether about a dozen organisations moved, not whether a market responded.

q3_manual_vs_automatic.method: Actions from delegation_change_clusters (month x source x block x transition). Matching transitions: sign or rollover to the algorithm the default names. Window: ledger labels r+1..r+4 for a release in calendar month r, i.e. the changes made in the release month and the 3 months after. Statistics: difference, window minus other months, in the share of matching delegations moved in actions of >= 10 delegations, and in the share at level one block or concentrated (delegation_change_levels). Null: the same number of months drawn without replacement from the ledger span, 1000 draws; p = share of draws at or above the observed difference. Sensitivity: the same permutation restricted to months within +-36 months of the window (era-matched), because ledger activity rises about 25-fold from 2009 to 2019.
q3_manual_vs_automatic.proxy_caveat: Action size is a proxy. One operator automating one delegation is indistinguishable from a manual edit, and one operator hand-editing a block is indistinguishable from an upgrade.
q3_manual_vs_automatic.ledger_dating: Ledger label M = the change between the snapshots of 00:00 UTC on the 1st of M-1 and of M, so it happened in calendar month M-1. The window for a release in calendar month r is labels r+1..r+4, the changes of calendar months r..r+3.

q4_spikes.method: Spikes by program_rfc_cases.spikes() (imported, not re-implemented) on numerator counts: forward per TLD (floor 300), reverse per RIR (floor 30, counts only). A reverse spike labelled M is a change between the states of the 1st of M-1 and the 1st of M, so it happened in calendar month M-1; lags and chance rates use that calendar month. Both directions are scanned. A relevant default change maps to the same observable with the same expected direction; 'aligned' = one at 0..3 months before the spike start. Chance = share of the series' months that have a relevant default change 0..3 months before them. Beating chance is judged per observable, corpus and direction by the Poisson-binomial tail of the aligned count.
q4_spikes.forward_note: Forward corpus: earlier work found every forward adoption jump belonged to one of two registry operators, paired across that operator's TLDs, so a forward event study measures whether about a dozen organisations moved, not whether a market responded.

Peak = maximum over covered months with at least 300 in the denominator; months counted from the successor's publication to the first month after the peak below half of it. Descriptive only.
